# FDG9074

> DO implement the Basic Dispose Pattern on every finalizable type. See section 9.4.1 for details on the basic pattern.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.4.2 Finalizable Types.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9074, CA1063
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Implement the Basic Dispose Pattern on the finalizable type '{0}'

FDG9074 reports a finalizer declared in a class, of any accessibility, that does not implement IDisposable. CA1063 reports a finalizable class that implements IDisposable but whose finalizer does not call Dispose(false), and the other departures from the pattern listed for FDG9062; it honors api_surface, so the library profile checks externally visible types only (probe with SDK 10.0.402). The other parts of the pattern are FDG9064 to FDG9066. Implementing IDisposable adds to the public API without changing a signature, so autofix is no; there is no code fix.

## From the book

This gives users of the type a means to explicitly perform deterministic cleanup of those same resources for which the finalizer is responsible.

Consistent use of the Basic Dispose Pattern for internal finalizable types allows new developers of your library to transfer their skills between projects, and to better interact with the few public finalizable types in .NET.
